narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Gel-Lit Room"**

The app is a dark room at a party, and the only color in it is light. The ground is a deep blue-violet night; surfaces are slightly lifted dusk tones; text is moonlight. Each of the fifteen games owns one stage gel, and when a game is up the room turns that color: a wash spills down from the top of the screen, the primary button glows in it, the timer arc draws in it, the active seat is ringed in it. Leave the game and the light crossfades to the next one. Nothing on screen is colored for decoration.

Density is low and the type is big because the phone is a prop passed around a dim table, read at arm's length, tapped with one thumb. Every screen is bilingual: titles show both languages at once, the reader's language leading large and the other riding beneath it smaller, and a 中 / EN toggle switches every string in place. Motion is GSAP throughout, settled and weighted for ordinary moves, and saved up for the penalty, which is the loudest thing the app ever does: the room flashes, one huge word slams down, a glass slides in and drains.

When a game brings its own physical objects, they render as themselves inside the room: Euchre's playing cards are white card stock with real suit marks, lit from above by the jade gel.
keyCharacteristics: Night ground, moonlight text, one current gel per screen.
Color always means "this game" or "this state" (go, stop, warn, your turn).
Bilingual titles: both languages visible, the current one leads.
One primary action per screen, pill-shaped, 50 to 60px tall.
Settled GSAP motion; the penalty stamp is the single most animated moment.
Flat tonal surfaces with hairline insets; glow only comes from light.

rules.name: The Color Is Light Rule
rules.body: Every hue on screen comes from the current gel, the room light, or a signal. If a color can't answer "which game, or which state?", it does not belong.

rules.name: The Bright Gel Rule
rules.body: Gels carry Night text, never white. A gel faded or desaturated reads as mud on the night ground; a resting primary goes to Dusk High with Fog text instead of dimming its gel.

rules.name: The Red Is The Penalty Rule
rules.body: Stop Red appears on the penalty stamp, the button that sends someone to it, the last ten seconds of a timer, and errors. Nowhere else.

rules.name: The Both Languages Rule
rules.body: A title shows Chinese and English together. The reader's language leads in the display face; the other follows in Haze at roughly half size (16/12, 24/14, 34/16). Body strings switch with the toggle.

rules.name: The Tabular Count Rule
rules.body: Anything that ticks (seconds, scores, counts) uses tabular figures.

rules.name: The Light Casts The Glow Rule
rules.body: A glow is always the gel or signal color of the thing that emits it. Neutral glows, and glows on things that are not lit, do not exist here.

dos: Do take every hue from the current gel (`--gel`), the room light (`--light`), or a signal (`--go`, `--stop`, `--warn`).
Do set `--gel` on any container that belongs to a game, and call `setLight()` when a screen changes, so the room crossfades.
Do put Night text on gels and Moonlight text on dusk surfaces.
Do show every title in both languages, the reader's language leading in the display face.
Do keep one primary (gel) button per screen, 50px or taller, near the bottom.
Do animate with GSAP on the house `settle` ease (`0.16, 1, 0.3, 1`, 0.5s default) and check `reduced()` before every tween, jumping straight to the end state when it is true.
Do keep the penalty stamp the most animated moment on any screen; everything else settles.
Do use lucide icons or authored SVG; playing-card suit marks are the cards' own text.
donts: Don't color anything for decoration: no off-palette accents, no second accent beside the gel.
Don't dim or desaturate a gel for a disabled state; use Dusk High with Fog text.
Don't use Stop Red outside the penalty, its trigger button, a timer's last ten seconds, and errors.
Don't add neutral drop shadows or glows; depth is tonal layering plus light the gel casts.
Don't put uppercase tracked labels or eyebrows above headings; uppercase tracking is for table codes only.
